subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm designing a jaguar-eagle alebrije hybrid, combining a jaguar body with eagle wings, head, and feathered tail, decorated with bright dots, stripes, and swirls, while keeping the implementation compact but robust.

Still defining the skeleton...

Varying body radii with simple tapering arrays, then adding a feather ruff around the neck base using a ring of spike shapes with cycling colors. For the eagle head, I'm sculpting a scaled skull sphere and starting on the beak shape.

Now I'm sweeping a curved bezier path for the upper beak with yellow coloring and taper, and a shorter lower beak attached at a jaw joint. For the eyes I'm placing symmetric decals on the skull with round SVG eye textures and ring details, plus thinking about a brow ridge.

Adding a feather crest along the head and small round jaguar-style ears on top, then working out the four-legged limb rig: front legs bending backward at the elbow, hind legs with three segments bending forward at the knee and back at the hock, positioning hips and feet so leg lengths match the needed stance distances.

Now I'm designing the paws as a hybrid — jaguar paw base with eagle-talon claws, placing a flattened sphere at the foot position and adding three forward-curving claw spikes off the toe area.

Now I'm laying out the wing joint chains, defining root, elbow, wrist, and tip positions for each side to create spread, partly-raised eagle wings extending back from the shoulders.

Shaping flight feathers...

Working out wing joint attachment using the chain's bone and position data, confirming wings mirror correctly via sign-based x-offsets in model coordinates. Now moving on to planning a long, curled jaguar tail.

Defining the tail chain...

Let me fix the orientation: width axis along x=d within the xy plane, thickness axis perpendicular to d also in the xy plane, so the feather stands facing the viewer as a flat fan seen from behind.

I'll place 7 feathers spread across -60 to 60 degrees around the up axis for the tail fan. I'm also assigning spine roles to the hip and spine chains, then scattering small flattened discs across the body as alebrije-style spots, plus adding decal textures like eyes and a flower emblem on the flank.

Figuring out the decal placement math for the flank flower so it lands correctly based on left/right side orientation, and settling on a final texture set: eye, flower, and maybe a step-fret pattern for the legs.

Settling on four textures total: eye, flower, a forehead diamond, and a spiral motif for the thighs, with decal positioning tied to each limb's local coordinate frame. Now I'm defining the folk-art color scheme, starting with an orange base with blue, pink, and green spot accents layered through a countershading function.

Working out the neck stripes in teal with pink and yellow bands, and sketching a simple head paint with turquoise base and yellow cheek patches via a custom gradient function. Then I'm laying out leg rings in orange with contrasting stripes, and finalizing the folk palette with hex values for orange, pink, teal, blue, yellow, and green.

Now I'm shaping the skull geometry as a scaled sphere and building the beak as a bezier sweep from the head's local space -- defining base, control, and tip points, giving it a yellow hooked shape with an orange cere, then adding a lower jaw piece with its own bone and capsule joint.

For nostrils, I'm placing small dark spheres near the beak's top surface, using a nearest-point search to stick them onto the curved geometry accurately rather than guessing coordinates blindly. Now I'm moving on to placing eye decals on the skull.

Placing the brow capsules near the skull surface as a ridge, then adding a row of spikes across the top of the head forming a crest.

Still working out head details... adding jaguar ear spheres with orange coloring and pink inner accents, then starting a neck ruff made from a ring of spikes placed along the chain's frame points.

Scaling hip and shoulder joints for chunkiness, adding cream belly countershading, and verifying ground contact so paws and leg tubes sit flush at y=0 with total height around 1.5. Now I'm working out the limb function signature that takes root, target, lengths, and bend parameters to build each leg procedurally.

Defining leg sweep geometry with tapered radii and striped paint along the y-axis, plus a similar sweep for the wings with thinner tapering radii. I'm also sketching a feather helper function that extrudes a flat outline oriented by direction and a vertical up-vector for the wing feathers.

For the wing feather placement, I'm working out direction vectors that angle outward for primaries near the tip and curve back for secondaries near the elbow, with feather length scaling along the wing parameter t, all sampled along the wing's arm path and bound to the appropriate bone.

I'm planning two layers of flight feathers - ten main feathers cycling through pink, blue, teal, yellow, red, and ten shorter covert feathers offset slightly upward and forward with different colors - plus adding small contrasting tip overlays on each feather for extra visual detail. I'll apply the same tip-feather trick to the tail fan, and set the wing pose to a partially raised position.

Adjusting the wing joint points so the root, elbow, wrist, and tip curve upward more dramatically for a raised wing stance, then adding flower decals onto the body surface. Finally I'm scattering small colored dot discs across the skin surface using a scatter function with minimum distance and normal filtering, embedding tiny cylinders as spots that can overlap the existing decals for a layered, textured look.
